content: 1. Drospirenone has a minor interaction with ergotamine, potentially increasing its levels or effects by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Drospirenone may also increase the levels or effects of erlotinib through a similar mechanism involving CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains unclear. 3. Erythromycin base can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of erythromycin base by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is uncertain. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral hormone forms and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 9. Erythromycin stearate can reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 11. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of escitalopram by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. 12. Eslicarbazepine acetate can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative drugs or additional nonhormonal birth control methods should be used. 13. Both drospirenone and esmolol can increase serum potassium levels. Close monitoring and potential therapy modification are necessary. 14. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of esomeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 15. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 16. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 17. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 18. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of estropipate through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 19. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of eszopiclone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 20. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while ethacrynic acid decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, and caution is advised. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 22. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ethosuximide through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 23. Both drospirenone and etodolac can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 24. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of etoposide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 25. Etravirine can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of etravirine through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 27. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain. 28. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of exemestane via CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be coadministered with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. Alternative drugs should be used. 29. Ethinyl estradiol and exenatide injectable solution may interact, as oral contraceptives can impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Ethinyl estradiol and exenatide injectable suspension may interact similarly. Patients should be advised to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Fedratinib may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of fedratinib. Coadministration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided. Alternative drugs are recommended. 33. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fedratinib through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 34. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of felbamate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Felbamate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 35. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of felodipine via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Both drospirenone and fenbufen can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fenofibrate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unclear. 38. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fenofibrate micronized through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fenofibric acid by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 40. Both drospirenone and fenoprofen can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fentanyl by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 42. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fentanyl intranasal, transdermal, or transmucosal forms via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 43. Fexinidazole may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP2E1 metabolism. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Alternative drugs should be used. 44. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Fezolinetant plasma concentrations are increased when coadministered with CYP1A2 inhibitors. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Both drospirenone and finerenone can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Finerenone dosage adjustments should be based on serum potassium levels. 46. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments. 47. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of finerenone through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 48. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of flibanserin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flibanserin via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 50. Fluconazole may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flunisolide inhaled by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 52. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flurazepam through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 53. Both drospirenone and flurbiprofen can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 54. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flutamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 55. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate or inhaled fluticasone via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 56. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while formoterol decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, and caution is recommended. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 58. Forskolin may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unclear. 59. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol and fosamprenavir coadministration may alter hormone levels and decrease amprenavir AUC, potentially leading to virologic failure. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 60. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fosaprepitant via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 61. Drospirenone and fosinopril may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia. Caution and monitoring are advised. 62. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fostamatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 63. Fostemsavir may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Ethinyl estradiol doses should not exceed 30 mcg/day. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 64. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of frovatriptan by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 65. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while furosemide decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, and caution is advised. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 66. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of gefitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 67. Gemifloxacin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 68. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, and caution is advised. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 69. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of glasdegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 70. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 71. Goldenrod may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical relevance is unknown. 72. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
